rendered: The anode-free full cell uses pyrite (FeS2) as its cathode, paired with carbon/Al current collectors.[1] Because pyrite natively contains no sodium, it is presodiated before cell assembly, in a fashion similar to previous reports, so the cell is built in a discharged state.[2][3] Sodium metal is therefore not present on assembly: during the initial charge, sodium ions leave the pyrite and are reduced on the carbon/Al current collector to form sodium metal in situ.[4][5] For the cathode capacity, the energy density was calculated on the mass of the presodiated pyrite, assuming a Na1.5FeS2 stoichiometry[6] and a FeS2 capacity of 335 mAh/g[7], giving the roughly ∼400 Wh/kg[8] energy density reported.
